scenes.tts: A starburst cell has branches pointing every way. Which ones inhibit a given ganglion cell?
scenes.visual: Title card: Reading the Wiring. A starburst cell with many spokes beside a gold ganglion cell; question marks on the spokes.
scenes.narration: A starburst cell has branches pointing every way. Which ones inhibit a given ganglion cell?

scenes.tts: In two thousand two, Euler, Detwiler and Denk imaged calcium in single starburst dendrites, in rabbit retina.
scenes.caption: In 2002, Euler, Detwiler and Denk imaged calcium in single starburst dendrites, in rabbit retina.
scenes.visual: Label: Euler, Detwiler and Denk, 2002, isolated rabbit retina, two-photon calcium imaging.
scenes.narration: In 2002, Euler, Detwiler and Denk imaged calcium in single starburst dendrites, in rabbit retina.

scenes.tts: A dendrite gave larger calcium signals for motion outward from the cell body than for motion inward.
scenes.visual: One dendrite: a large calcium trace for outward motion, a small one for inward motion.
scenes.narration: A dendrite gave larger calcium signals for motion outward from the cell body than for motion inward.

scenes.tts: Predict. The cell body sits where all the branches meet. What should its voltage show?
scenes.visual: The soma at the hub of four spokes, with an empty voltage readout. On screen: what does the soma show?
scenes.narration: Predict. The cell body sits where all the branches meet. What should its voltage show?

scenes.tts: Little preference. Motion outward along one branch runs inward along the branch opposite it.
scenes.visual: A rightward spot: the right-pointing spoke lights, the left-pointing spoke dims. Arrows for the four spoke preferences.
scenes.narration: Little preference. Motion outward along one branch runs inward along the branch opposite it.

scenes.tts: A soma that simply summed equal spokes would see them cancel. The measured somatic voltage did not show the dendrites' preference.
scenes.visual: The four spoke arrows, each standing for that branch's directional modulation (not a calcium level), slide head to tail and sum to nearly zero. Label: soma, little preference, under the conditions tested.
scenes.narration: A soma that simply summed equal spokes would see them cancel. The measured somatic voltage did not show the dendrites' preference.

scenes.tts: So the branch, not the cell, is the unit. Each branch has its own preferred direction, set by where it points.
scenes.visual: Each spoke gets its own outward arrow. Label: the branch is the unit.
scenes.narration: So the branch, not the cell, is the unit. Each branch has its own preferred direction, set by where it points.

scenes.tts: One limit here. A calcium signal is not transmitter release.
scenes.visual: Small caption on screen: calcium is a proxy, not release.
scenes.narration: One limit here. A calcium signal is not transmitter release.

scenes.tts: In that simple sum, input taken equally from every branch carries no direction signal. So the wiring should be selective.
scenes.visual: A ganglion cell connected to all four spokes: its inhibition bars for left and right motion are equal.
scenes.narration: In that simple sum, input taken equally from every branch carries no direction signal. So the wiring should be selective.

scenes.tts: Paired recordings in rabbit had shown it. Branches pointing in a ganglion cell's null direction inhibited it, and preferred-pointing branches did not.
scenes.visual: Label: Fried, Münch and Werblin, 2002, paired recordings, rabbit. A null-pointing branch delivers an inhibitory current; a preferred-pointing branch delivers none.
scenes.narration: Paired recordings in rabbit had shown it. Branches pointing in a ganglion cell's null direction inhibited it, and preferred-pointing branches did not.

scenes.tts: In two thousand eleven, Briggman, Helmstaedter and Denk read the wiring directly, in mouse retina.
scenes.caption: In 2011, Briggman, Helmstaedter and Denk read the wiring directly, in mouse retina.
scenes.visual: Label: Briggman, Helmstaedter and Denk, 2011, wild-type mouse retina.
scenes.narration: In 2011, Briggman, Helmstaedter and Denk read the wiring directly, in mouse retina.

scenes.tts: First they imaged calcium during moving bars, to find each ganglion cell's preferred direction.
scenes.visual: Moving bars sweep across a field of ganglion cells; each gets a coloured preferred arrow.
scenes.narration: First they imaged calcium during moving bars, to find each ganglion cell's preferred direction.

scenes.tts: Then they cut the same tissue for electron microscopy, and traced the cells and their contacts.
scenes.visual: The same tissue becomes a stack of electron microscopy sections; cells are traced through it into a reconstruction.
scenes.narration: Then they cut the same tissue for electron microscopy, and traced the cells and their contacts.

scenes.tts: Predict. Take a cell that prefers rightward motion. Which way should its contacting branches point?
scenes.visual: A rightward-preferring gold cell with starburst branches around it, uncoloured. On screen: which way do the contacting branches point?
scenes.narration: Predict. Take a cell that prefers rightward motion. Which way should its contacting branches point?

scenes.tts: Most starburst input came from branches pointing roughly left, in the null direction.
scenes.visual: A polar plot of contacts clusters on the left, the null direction, opposite the preferred arrow.
scenes.narration: Most starburst input came from branches pointing roughly left, in the null direction.

scenes.tts: And the direction of the individual branch predicted contact better than the line between cell bodies.
scenes.visual: Branch-direction rule lights as the better predictor; the soma-to-soma line dims.
scenes.narration: And the direction of the individual branch predicted contact better than the line between cell bodies.

scenes.tts: One limit. A contact shows wiring, not synaptic strength.
scenes.visual: Caption: contacts show wiring, not strength.
scenes.narration: One limit. A contact shows wiring, not synaptic strength.

scenes.tts: So the picture holds. Most starburst contacts come from branches pointing roughly in the cell's null direction.
scenes.visual: Return to the circuit picture: mostly left-pointing spokes connected to the rightward-preferring cell with gold synapse dots, a few faint contacts from other spokes.
scenes.narration: So the picture holds. Most starburst contacts come from branches pointing roughly in the cell's null direction.
